messages.author: 71e0c79dc1f92efe
messages.subject: Itemfit -  Empirical plots - itemGAM
parts:
Hi Phil and MIRT community

I have been working with MIRT, the purpose of my analysis is to fit a unidimensional graded model to a Likert scale dataset of ~340.000 individuals and more than 20 items, my data has structural voids, however, there are 3 common items. I have several questions (I have been studying for a long period of time, but until now, I don't have a satisfactory answer)

1. I run itemFit to compute item-fit statistics (X2*, S_X2, X2*_df, PV_Q1, PV_Q1*), I had some errors because the cases were not complete(my mistake). However, when the function runs properly, the results are that most of the items are misfitted. I read that those statistics are sensible to large databases, so I run again with many samples (n = 100, n = 200, n = 300, ..., n = 1000). Additionally, those samples had completed cases(without structural voids), with those modifications, unfortunately, The problem of misfit remain.  Any idea of how to fix that, maybe another model? (I modeled the items with other itemtype like: grsm, grsmIRT, ggum, spline - I create dummy items for that model - ) 

mod0 <- try(mirt(datAnaCalifica,  1, itemtype = "graded", method = 'EM', SE = TRUE))
mod1 <- try(mirt(datAnaCalifica,  1, itemtype = "grsm", method = 'EM', SE = TRUE))
mod2 <- try(mirt(datAnaCalifica,  1, itemtype = "grsmIRT", method = 'EM', SE = TRUE))
mod3 <- try(mirt(datAnaCalifica,  1, itemtype = "ggum", method = 'EM', SE = TRUE))
mod7 <- try(mirt(datAnaCalifica1, 1, itemtype = "spline", method = 'EM', SE = TRUE))

, so for that reason is my second question...

2. I inspected the empirical plots, however, is not clear for me how to check if I can admit the misfit that was identified previously ( I think the issue could be the category 4, I was thinking to collapse that category with the category 5).



3. There is a way to save those plots? I tried with the following functions but the result was unsatisfactory (jpeg, png)
4. Finally, I used itemGAM function to estimate response curves for items that do not seem to fit well in a given model. The first graph was fit with 10 nodes, and the second with 20 nodes. The first plot makes me think that every is O.K (Do you agree with me?), but the second shows a misfit 






Thank you for your help!
   Ana

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Itemfit - Empirical plots - itemGAM
parts:
There's isn't always a way to save poorly fitting items. The functional forms could be quite complex, non-monotonic, contain step functions, and so on. So sometimes, we just have to admit that some items do not fit well, and ask whether their inclusion is still justifiable even with some misfit. That said, I don't see a huge problem with this item in terms of the point-wise diagnostics. As well, so long as the RMSEA for the SX2 statistic is reasonably low relative to the other items then you may be justified in keeping it in your test. Probably not the most exacting advice you wanted to hear :) 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Itemfit - Empirical plots - itemGAM
parts:
I don't think I'd give a hard cut-off, in my original sentence I just said "reasonably low relative to the other items". For more reasonable cut-offs I think someone would need to run an intensive Monte Carlo simulation....though even then I'd be skeptical, as I am of all cut-offs that have appeared in the SEM literature.

Phil
